metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Passaic County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Cupsaw Lake & Erskine Lakes Section, Stonetown & Skyline Drive Enclave
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 4.259%, with an equalization ratio of 61.68%.
Public education represents 61.4% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 23.8%.
Average residential assessment is $320,736, producing an average annual tax bill of $13,660.15.

neighborhoods.name: Cupsaw Lake & Erskine Lakes Section
neighborhoods.character: Wooded private lake community with private beaches, clubhouses, custom rustic ranches, and log-cabin style colonials
neighborhoods.description: Scenic lakeside mountain community situated in the Ramapo Mountains adjacent to Ringwood State Park and Skylands Manor.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: High reliance on residential ratables due to extensive state-owned parkland and watershed protection zones (Highlands Act).

neighborhoods.name: Stonetown & Skyline Drive Enclave
neighborhoods.character: Rustic mountain retreats, custom log homes, and acreage properties nestled deep in Ramapo mountain passes
neighborhoods.description: Secluded Highlands enclave offering mountain privacy, hiking trails, and horse properties.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Low service density with well water and private septic systems.

equityAnalysis.summary: Ringwood Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Ringwood Borough, homeowners pay an average of $13,660.15 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 10.18% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 61.68%, assessed values average ~61.68% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 61.4% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 23.8%, and Passaic County claims 14.8%.
